data.reasoning: The deepseek report successfully reviewed all 4 files and found standard DKMS packaging practices: PKGBUILD contains only variable definitions with no dangerous top-level code, sources from the maintainer's own GitHub repository, .install script performs expected service/module lifecycle management, and the systemd service is a standard tmpfiles configuration. No injection patterns, no execution of fetched content, no fetching from unrelated hosts. The qwen report failed due to API errors on 3 of 4 files, providing no usable verdict signal.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement stems from tool failure, not analytical disagreement. The qwen model experienced HTTP 400 errors when attempting to audit .SRCINFO, PKGBUILD, and linuwu-sense-setup.service, leaving only linuwu-sense.install reviewed. The deepseek model successfully completed all file reviews and found no issues. This is not a true disagreement but rather a coverage gap in one report.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to audit 3 of 4 files (.SRCINFO, PKGBUILD, linuwu-sense-setup.service) due to HTTP 400 API errors
learnings: API errors during audit should be clearly distinguished from analytical findings - the qwen report's 'inconclusive' status was due to tool failure, not package ambiguity
When one model fails due to infrastructure issues, a successful review from another model covering the same files should be sufficient for verdict
Standard DKMS packages with VCS sources (git+) and SKIP checksums are common and should not trigger concern when the source is the maintainer's own repository
